q: Is there a way to make Git automatically replay a conflict fix I already made once, when the same conflict shows up again during repeated rebases?
a: Yes: enable rerere (reuse recorded resolution), e.g. git config --global rerere.enabled true; Git records resolutions and reapplies them.
ev: The configuration setting is `rerere.enabled`

q: What are the advantages of serving a Git repository over SSH?
a: Easy to set up (SSH daemons are common), secure (encrypted and authenticated transfer), and efficient (compact data).
ev: access over SSH is secure -- all data transfer is encrypted and authenticated

q: How can I give teammates push access to a repository on a server where they don't have their own user accounts?
a: You must set up SSH access for them, e.g. accounts for everyone or a single shared git user with their keys.
ev: then you must set up SSH access for them

q: Where can I see the full list of configuration options that my installed Git version understands?
a: Run man git-config (or the git-config docs on git-scm.com).
ev: $ man git-config

q: When migrating a repository from Subversion, how do I turn SVN usernames into proper Git author names and emails?
a: Create a users.txt file mapping each SVN user to a Git name and email and pass it to the import.
ev: Create a file called `users.txt` that has this mapping

q: What does git pull actually do compared with git fetch?
a: fetch only downloads data without touching the working directory; pull is essentially fetch followed by merge of the tracked remote branch.
ev: `git pull` which is essentially a `git fetch` immediately followed by a `git merge`

q: Why doesn't Git try harder to resolve merge conflicts automatically?
a: Its philosophy is to be smart when a resolution is unambiguous but not to try to be clever about resolving real conflicts.
ev: it does not try to be clever about automatically resolving it

q: Someone committed a very large file long ago and deleted it in the next commit; why are clones still huge?
a: Clone downloads the whole history, and the file stays reachable in history, so every clone downloads it.
ev: every clone for all time will be forced to download that large file

q: Why can't the dumb HTTP transfer protocol be used to push changes?
a: It cannot handle writing data from client to server; the smart protocol with a remote process is needed.
ev: it can't handle writing of data from the client to the server

q: Can a GitHub pull request be opened against another pull request instead of the main branch?
a: Yes, a PR can target any branch in the network, including another pull request, via the Edit button on the target box.
ev: you can even target another Pull Request

q: Where in a GitHub repository do you set up webhooks and third-party service integrations?
a: In the repository Settings, under the Webhooks and Services tab.

q: What's the practical difference between a pull request coming from a fork and one from a branch in the same repository?
a: With forks you usually cannot push to each other's branches; with internal PRs both parties can access the branch.
ev: the ones in a fork are often from people where you can't push to their branch

q: What is the difference between a module's interface and its dependencies?
a: The interface is the part visible to other modules; dependencies are the other modules it uses.
ev: The interface is the part of the module that's visible to other modules

q: How do I draw text on an HTML canvas and choose its size and typeface?
